title: QC - Councils, Committees & Partnerships - 001 - Sectoral Committees and Business Councils
description:
FRONTEND — Visitor Display
User Story ID: QC-001 |
US-026 | REF: FR-026
Title: Sectoral Committees
and Business Councils — Visitor Display
As a public website visitor
I want to navigate to the
Sectoral Committees and Business Councils page, review the leadership directory
and the full list of committees, and access the correct request form
So that I can learn about
committee structures, their mandates, and submit the appropriate joining or
feedback request
Preconditions
- The Qatar Chamber website is published and accessible.
- The Sectoral Committees and Business Councils page is published
in the CMS.
- At least one committee entry and the Head of Sectoral
Committees leadership card are active and published.
- The Committee Joining Request, Business Council Joining
Request, and Suggestions and Complaints pages are published and reachable.
What the Visitor Sees
- Breadcrumb (Home › Councils, Committees &
Partnerships), and a hero banner titled “Sectoral Committees and Business
Councils” with the eyebrow “Committees & Business Councils” and the
subtitle “Explore Qatar Chamber's sectoral committees, understand their
responsibilities, and access the appropriate joining or feedback request.”
- A “Sector representation” section with the heading
“Where business insight informs action,” introductory text, and a single
expandable card labeled “Leadership directory › Head of Sectoral committees ›
View committee leaders and the sectors they represent.”
- When expanded, the Head of Sectoral Committees card
reveals a grid of 12 leader cards, each showing a Number, the leader's Name,
and the Committee/Sector they represent (see Field-Level Details).
- A “Committee directory” section with the heading
“Explore the Committees,” introductory text, and a search field placeholder
“Search by committee or sector.”
- A list of 12 committees, each row showing a Number (01–12),
the Committee Name, and a short one-line description, with an expand/collapse
control.
- Expanding a committee row (e.g., Banking &
Investment Committee) reveals the eyebrow “Committee competencies,” the heading
“Mandate and responsibilities,” and a checklist of that committee's specific
mandate items. Every committee in the directory follows this same eyebrow /
heading / checklist structure, with mandate content unique to that committee.
- A highlighted “Continue with Qatar Chamber” panel with
the eyebrow “Continue with Qatar Chamber,” heading “Choose the appropriate
request,” and introductory text, followed by three CTA cards: “Committee
Joining Request,” “Business Council Joining Request,” and “Suggestions and
Complaints,” each with an icon, short description, and an arrow/navigate
control.
Frontend Workflow
- Public Visitor navigates to Main Menu → Councils,
Committees & Partnerships → Sectoral Committees and Business Councils.
- Page loads with the hero banner and the “Sector
representation” section, showing the Head of Sectoral Committees card in its
collapsed state.
- Visitor clicks the Head of Sectoral Committees card to
expand it; the grid of 12 leader cards (Number, Name, Committee/Sector) is
displayed. Clicking the card's close control collapses it again.
- Visitor scrolls to the “Explore the Committees” section
and views the list of all 12 committees with their number, name, and short
description.
- Visitor optionally types into the “Search by committee
or sector” field; the list filters to matching committees by name or sector
keyword. The search filter is applied independently of each committee section's
expand or collapse state — a visitor can search whether a given committee section
is currently expanded or collapsed, and the filtered results are unaffected by
prior expand/collapse interactions.
- Visitor clicks a committee row to expand it; the
section reveals the “Committee competencies” eyebrow, the “Mandate and
responsibilities” heading, and that committee's mandate checklist. Clicking the
row's close control collapses it again.
- Visitor scrolls to the “Continue with Qatar Chamber”
panel and clicks one of the three CTAs — “Committee Joining Request,” “Business
Council Joining Request,” or “Suggestions and Complaints” — the system
navigates the visitor to the corresponding webform page.
Acceptance Criteria
Given
the visitor opens the Sectoral Committees and Business Councils page
When
the visitor interacts with the leadership card, the committee list,
the search field, or a CTA
Then:
- the system shall display the hero banner, the Sector
Representation section, the Committee Directory section, and the Continue with
Qatar Chamber panel in the configured order.
- the Head of Sectoral Committees card shall expand to
show a grid of leader cards (Number, Name, Committee/Sector) and collapse on
demand.
- the Committee Directory list shall display all active
committees with Number, Name, and short description, in the CMS-configured
display order.
- the search field shall filter the committee list by
committee name or sector keyword, regardless of any section's current
expand/collapse state.
- clicking a committee row shall expand it to reveal its
Committee competencies eyebrow, Mandate and responsibilities heading, and
mandate checklist; clicking again shall collapse it.
- each of the three CTA cards (Committee Joining Request,
Business Council Joining Request, Suggestions and Complaints) shall navigate
the visitor to its respective webform page on click.
- only published leader cards, committee entries, and CTA
cards are visible to the public visitor.
- the page and all accordion interactions function
correctly on desktop, tablet, and mobile.
Edge Case Scenarios
- If a search keyword matches no committee name or
sector, the list displays an empty/no-results state.
- If a CTA's target link is misconfigured, the card
renders but navigation may fail (CMS admin responsibility).
Negative Scenarios
- A committee entry with an empty name or missing mandate
content cannot be saved by the CMS admin.
- A CTA card with an empty title or missing target link
cannot be published by the CMS admin.
Post Condition
Visitor successfully reviews the
Head of Sectoral Committees, explores committee mandates via the accordion
list, and navigates to the correct request form (Committee Joining Request,
Business Council Joining Request, or Suggestions and Complaints).
BACKEND — Admin CMS Management
User Story ID: QC-001 |
US-026 | REF: FR-026
Title: Sectoral Committees
and Business Councils — CMS Management
As an authorized admin user
(Site Content Editor / Site Content Author)
I want to manage the page's hero
banner, the Head of Sectoral Committees leadership cards, the Committee
Directory entries and their mandate content, and the Continue with Qatar
Chamber CTA cards
So that Qatar Chamber can keep
committee and business council information accurate and up to date for website
visitors
Administrator Workflow
- Site Content Editor or Site Content Author logs into
the Liferay CMS administration panel.
- Navigates to the Sectoral Committees and Business
Councils page.
- Manages page-level content: breadcrumb label, hero
title, hero subtitle, and hero background image (EN | AR).
- Manages the Sector Representation section: section
eyebrow, heading, subtext, and the Head of Sectoral Committees card copy (EN |
AR).
- Manages the Head of Sectoral Committees leader cards:
adds, edits, reorders, enables, or disables entries, each with Number, Leader
Name, and Committee/Sector Name (EN | AR).
- Manages the Committee Directory section: section
eyebrow, heading, subtext, and the search field placeholder text (EN | AR).
- Manages each committee entry: Display Order, Committee
Name, Short Description, and the mandate checklist shown when the entry is
expanded (Committee competencies eyebrow, Mandate and responsibilities heading,
and repeatable mandate bullet items, EN | AR); adds, edits, reorders, enables,
or disables entries.
- Manages the Continue with Qatar Chamber panel: panel
eyebrow, heading, subtext, and the three CTA cards (icon, title, description,
target link, EN | AR).
- Saves content as draft or previews it in website
format.
- Publishes the page; updated content becomes immediately
visible to website visitors.
Acceptance Criteria
Given
the admin is logged into Liferay CMS with appropriate permissions
When
the admin publishes the Sectoral Committees and Business Councils
page
Then:
- the admin can add, edit, reorder, enable, or disable
Head of Sectoral Committees leader cards.
- the admin can add, edit, reorder, enable, or disable
committee entries, including their mandate checklist content.
- the admin can add, edit, reorder, enable, or disable
the three Continue with Qatar Chamber CTA cards.
- only published leader cards, committee entries, and CTA
cards are visible to website visitors, in the configured display order.
- each committee entry must contain at least a committee
name and one mandate bullet item.
- each CTA card must contain a title and a valid target
link before it can be published.
- the system displays the Liferay generic toast after
each publish action.
only users with appropriate CMS
role permissions can create, edit, reorder, or delete leader cards, committee
entries, or CTA cards.
Negative Scenarios
- Publishing the hero without a title (EN or AR) triggers
a validation error.
- Publishing a committee entry without a name or without
at least one mandate bullet item triggers a validation error.
- Publishing a CTA card without a title or without a
target link triggers a validation error.
Post Condition
The Head of Sectoral Committees
leadership grid, the Committee Directory with its mandate checklists, and the
Continue with Qatar Chamber CTA cards are published and visible to website
visitors in the configured order.

Business Rules
- Only published Head of Sectoral Committees leader
cards, committee entries, and CTA cards are visible on the website.
- Leader cards and committee entries must appear
according to the display order configured by the CMS admin.
- Each committee entry must contain at least a committee
name and one mandate bullet item before it can be published.
- Each CTA card must contain a title and a valid target
link before it can be published.
- The search field filters the Committee Directory list
by committee name or sector keyword; filtering is applied independently of each
committee section's expand or collapse state.
- All three CTA cards must always navigate to their
configured target webform page on click; a card with no valid target link
cannot be published.
- Only users with appropriate CMS permissions can create,
edit, reorder, or delete leader cards, committee entries, or CTA cards.
- The Head of Sectoral Committees grid, the Committee
Directory list, and their expand/collapse interactions support desktop, tablet,
and mobile.
- All page-level and repeatable content (hero, sector
representation, committee directory, mandate checklists, CTA panel) is fully
bilingual (EN | AR) and CMS-configurable without code changes.
This page has
no direct form submission of its own — it is a CMS-managed directory/landing
page. Its three CTA cards route visitors to the Committee Joining Request,
Business Council Joining Request, and Suggestions and Complaints webforms, each
governed by its own user story (including CAPTCHA and the
Pending/Approve/Reject admin workflow). Arabic text on this page follows the
same right-to-left, complex-script font handling used across the other
Councils, Committees & Partnerships user stories.
